memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Depression.
Patient reports low mood, anhedonia, fatigue, and poor sleep for 3 months. Appears tearful, psychomotor retardation mild. PHQ-9 to be sent. No suicidal ideation. Initiate sertraline 50 mg OD.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been feeling down all the time, can’t enjoy work at the jewellery shop, and I’m sleeping poorly.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Depression, partial response.
Mood improved somewhat, still reports low energy and occasional insomnia. Sertraline tolerated but mild nausea. Consider switching to escitalopram.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
escitalopram 10 mg OD
sertraline taper off over 7 days

memories.author: lab
memories.text: PHQ-9: 12. TSH: 3.8 µIU/mL. Vitamin B12: 225 pg/mL.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow‑up appointment booked for 2025-10-10 at 10:00 with Dr Menon.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Depression, improving.
Patient reports better mood and sleep on escitalopram, but early morning awakening persists. Add mirtazapine 15 mg at night for sleep aid.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
escitalopram 10 mg OD
mirtazapine 15 mg HS

memories.author: lab
memories.text: PHQ-9: 8. TSH: 3.5 µIU/mL. Vitamin B12: 240 pg/mL.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Depression, stable.
Mood good, reports mild daytime drowsiness from mirtazapine. Reduce mirtazapine to 7.5 mg HS to lessen sedation.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
escitalopram 10 mg OD
mirtazapine 7.5 mg HS

memories.author: lab
memories.text: PHQ-9: 6. TSH: 3.2 µIU/mL. Vitamin B12: 250 pg/mL.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Depression, well controlled.
Patient euthymic, energetic, sleeping well. No side effects. Continue current regimen.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
escitalopram 10 mg OD
mirtazapine 7.5 mg HS

memories.author: lab
memories.text: PHQ-9: 5. TSH: 3.0 µIU/mL. Vitamin B12: 260 pg/mL.
